chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī Naṣr, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: concerning

A man who killed another man intentionally, then fled, and it was not possible to apprehend him until he died. He عليه السلام said: “If he has wealth, it shall be taken from it; otherwise, it shall be taken from the nearest relative, then the nearest.”

key_terms.الْأَقْرَبِ فَالْأَقْرَبِ: the nearest relative, then the nearest; order of familial financial responsibility
key_terms.مَاتَ: died; before punishment or enforcement could occur
key_terms.مَالٌ: wealth or property from which liability may be paid
key_terms.يُقْدَرْ عَلَيْهِ: be apprehended or overpowered; brought under legal control

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if an intentional killer flees and dies before he can be apprehended?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding intentional homicide when the killer escapes and dies before being apprehended. It states that financial liability is taken first from the killer’s estate, and if that is unavailable, then from his closest relatives in order of proximity.
